title: Progressive disclosure quicklaunch playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for a "progressive disclosure" quicklaunch experience for SDK users. Goal: get an engineer from zero to a meaningful local demo in <=10 minutes, then provide incremental, opt-in expansions (CLI, examples, telemetry, policy guardrails) so power users can level up without overwhelming beginners.

Audience / persona:
- Primary: backend/frontend engineers evaluating Redwood SDK for a feature prototype.
- Secondary: platform engineers who will integrate Redwood into CI, infra, or operators.

Success metrics (how we'll know it's working):
- Time-to-first-response median <= 8 minutes for new signups using quicklaunch flow (measured in lab kit telemetry).
- >50% conversion from quicklaunch to follow-up lab (opted into "level-up" flow) within 7 days for trial orgs.
- CI smoke tests based on quicklaunch sample pass rate >= 95% across main languages.

Design principles:
- Minimal blast radius: show the smallest working surface first (1 file, 1 command).
- Opt-in complexity: advanced features only appear after the user completes an explicit step.
- Local-first: make the first experience runnable entirely on the developer machine (no org-level configuration required).
- Repeatable labs: everything in the quicklaunch is scriptable for demo and CI.

Core flow (1 -> 2 -> 3 progressive stages)
1) Zero-friction start (0-5 mins):
   - Page/button: "Try quicklaunch" in Console SDK docs links to a single downloadable zip or 'curl | bash' bootstrap.
   - Outcome: a single example file that calls Redwood Hosted API and streams a short completion into stdout.
   - UX: no SDK install if using a tiny wrapper (curl bootstrap creates a virtualenv or installs a tiny distro binary).

   Minimal example (shown inline in the doc):
   - run: curl https://run.redwood.dev/quicklaunch | bash
   - that drops a folder: quicklaunch-demo/ and a run.sh that does one HTTP POST and prints response.

2) Guided exploration (5-20 mins):
   - After running the sample, the CLI prints: "Nice! Want to try a chat flow, embeddings, or tool calling? (y/n)".
   - If user opts in: a guided README opens with 3 short recipes (chat, summarization, embeddings+search) each in a single file.
   - Provide copy/paste prompts and small dataset (2–3 docs) for embeddings demo.

3) Level-up kit (20+ mins):
   - Optional modules: local debugging tips (enable verbose logs), canary rollout recipe, quota & cost check examples, telemetry integration with our SDK.
   - Includes: sample unit test (mocked sandbox), a Dockerfile for local sim, and a tiny Postman collection for manual testing.

Developer pathways (explicit map):
- Fast path: curl bootstrap -> run.sh -> success -> opt into sample chat -> DONE.
- Integrator path: Fast path -> add API key to env file -> run example CI job snippet -> validate usage telemetry -> schedule Dedicated trial.
- Research path: Fast path -> swap model config -> run perf script (latency/throughput) -> log parse for kernel hints.

Telemetry & instrumentation (what we record):
- Anonymous events in quicklaunch sandbox: step_started, step_completed, error_{type}, optin_level_up, lang_choice.
- Do not collect prompt text by default. If user enables opt-in telemetry for debugging, collect redacted prompt fingerprints only.
- Telemetry roadmap: wire events to a temporary trial dashboard in Console so growth/SDR can follow up if conversion signals look good.

Safety / policy guardrails:
- Samples must default to the smallest, safe completions (no code execution outside the local sandbox).
- Include a clear note: "This demo uses Hosted API: do not paste secrets into prompts."
- Provide a 'safe-mode' toggle in the quicklaunch bootstrap that strips external network calls from samples.

Docs surface and authoring guidelines:
- Microdocs: each recipe is a single-screen doc (200-400 words) with 3 sections: what it does, run it, next steps.
- Code-first examples in top languages: JS/TS, Python, Go, and a CLI shell wrapper. Keep each sample under ~60 LoC.
- Maintain a single source of truth in the repo: /quicklaunch/README.md is canonical; docs site pulls from it (CI link).

Lab exercises (for workshops/hackathons):
- Exercise 1 (5 min): Modify prompt to change answer style (concise -> persona).
- Exercise 2 (10 min): Add basic embeddings search over provided docs (3 files).
- Exercise 3 (15 min): Add a fallback policy that calls smaller model when latency > 500ms.

Troubleshooting quick hits (sticky checklist):
- If run.sh fails with 401: check REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in env (explain how to get it).
- If binary fails to execute: ensure permissions (chmod +x run.sh) and suggest using python -m venv fallback.
- If latency high locally: show how to enable sampling with local mock server to validate logic without cost.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should the bootstrap auto-open a browser to the Console trial page? (Pro: smoother conversion, Con: surprising network action).
- How aggressive should telemetry nudges be? Currently set to opt-in after first success.
- Language coverage: Rust? We propose to add a Rust minimal example after initial metrics.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Avery: prototype curl bootstrap and single-file run.sh (due 2026-03-20).
- Marcus: add telemetry events to staging infra and a small Console tile (due 2026-03-27).
- Sofia: write the three microdocs and workshop exercises (due 2026-03-24).
- Ravi: produce CI smoke script + Dockerfile and validate across mac/linux (due 2026-03-28).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the UX forgiving: errors should suggest copy/pasteable commands to recover.
- We want this to be scriptable for hackathon leads: add a --headless flag to the bootstrap.
- Consider a tiny 'telemetry playground' endpoint that shows anonymized funnel counts (internal only).

Appendix (useful links & snippets):
- Quick example: run.sh (pseudo):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -e
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY:-}
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","prompt":"Say hi"}' | jq -r .text

- CI snippet (bash): export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_STAGE_KEY && ./run.sh || exit 1

End of draft.

(If you read this and want to riff, leave notes inline — this doc is intentionally conversational and iterative.)
